title: Austin Approves Streetcar Line, Cocaine Regulation
summary:
• **Streetcar expansion approved**: The council voted to grant E.A. Ellis and associates the right to build and operate street railways along Austin streets, though the vote was close (11-10), indicating significant opposition to the project.

• **New cocaine sales regulations enacted**: Austin passed an ordinance restricting cocaine sales to physicians and dentists (dentists were added as an amendment), making it one of the early drug regulations in the city.

• **Property values declining**: The mayor reported that taxable property values dropped nearly $778,000 from the previous year to $10.75 million, prompting recommendations for a 1% general tax rate and a new 10-cent levy to fund street paving projects.

• **Water system testing requested**: The council approved forming a committee to test new filtering ditches at the city's water pumping station, though members disagreed on the scope and timeline of the evaluation.

• **City infrastructure investments authorized**: Council approved approximately $1,230 in spending for approved accounts and a new sanitary department cart, while also addressing dangerous bridge conditions requiring an estimated $4,500 in repairs.

Austin, Tex. Oct. 1898.
To the Honorable City Council:
As it was the understanding with the Committee from the City Council and Water Light and
